To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the human brain is organized into large-scale intrinsic networks that are active during task-free states; 2) these intrinsic networks can be reliably identified across individuals and are associated with distinct functional properties; 3) intrinsic brain networks can be used to predict the spatial distribution of neural activity in response to a wide range of tasks; and 4) the functional properties of intrinsic networks can be used as a basis for a domain-general architecture of the brain.
